_about: Reviewed fix steps, written and checked by people (not generated by the AI). Shown above every AI answer about a problem. Keep each step safe: no deleting data, no turning security off. Last reviewed: October 2026.

steps: Change the password to a long passphrase (4 or more random words, at least 14 characters). Use a different one for every system.
Turn on 2-step sign-in wherever it is offered (email, admin panels, remote access).
For SSH: set up key login first and test it in a second window, then turn off password login. Keep that second window open until you've confirmed you can still get in.
weakpw.verify: Press Scan now again. The problem should move to Verified fixes.

steps: Linux: run 'sudo apt update' and then 'sudo apt upgrade' (or 'sudo dnf upgrade'). Windows/macOS: open Settings and choose Software Update / Windows Update.
Turn on automatic security updates (Ubuntu: 'sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades').
Restart at a quiet time if the update asks for it.
outdated.verify: Press Scan now again after the restart.

steps: Install the waiting security updates now: 'sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade' on Ubuntu/Debian, Windows Update on Windows, Software Update on macOS.
If this machine runs something important (billing, records), do it outside working hours and make sure a backup exists first.
Restart if asked.
patches.verify: Press Scan now again. The number of waiting security patches should be 0.

steps: Find who can open the file, folder or service named in the problem.
Remove access for 'Everyone' or for people who no longer need it. Give access to named people or groups only.
If you're not sure what a permission does, don't change it: ask your IT person.
accesscontrol.verify: Press Scan now again, and ask a colleague to confirm they can still do their normal work.

steps: This is a problem in website or app code. Contact the developer or the company that made the app.
Until it's fixed, limit who can reach the page (for example staff network only).
Make sure the app is on its latest version.
sqli.verify: Ask the developer for proof the fix was tested, then scan again.

steps: This is a problem in website or app code. Contact the developer or vendor.
Update the app or plugin to its latest version.
Until it's fixed, warn staff not to click unexpected links to the site.
xss.verify: Ask the developer for proof the fix was tested, then scan again.

steps: Check whether the service named in the problem is actually needed. If not, turn it off in its settings or uninstall it.
If it is needed, allow it only from the machines that use it: Ubuntu 'sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port PORT', Windows Defender Firewall > Advanced settings > Inbound rules.
Turn on the firewall if it's off (Ubuntu: first 'sudo ufw allow OpenSSH' if you connect over SSH, then 'sudo ufw enable').
misconfig.verify: Press Scan now again. The port should no longer show as open to the network.

steps: List who has administrator rights (Linux: 'getent group sudo'; Windows: Settings > Accounts > Other users).
Keep administrator rights for 1 to 3 people who need them. Give everyone else a normal account.
Never remove the last administrator, and don't remove your own rights until another admin account is tested.
Make the service listen on this machine only (localhost) unless other machines really need it.
Turn on its login or access token setting, and use a long random key.
Block its port in the firewall from outside your network.
apis.verify: Press Scan now again. The service should show 'this machine only'.

steps: If nobody uses this remote access, turn it off (Windows: Settings > System > Remote Desktop; macOS: System Settings > General > Sharing).
If you need it, don't expose it to the internet: use a VPN, and allow it only from your office network.
Make sure every account that can use it has a strong password and 2-step sign-in.
remote.verify: Press Scan now again. Keep another way to reach the machine while you change this.

steps: Choose a backup tool (Windows: File History; macOS: Time Machine; Linux: Déjà Dup or restic).
Keep at least one copy somewhere else (another disk kept offline, or a cloud backup).
Once a month, restore one file to prove the backup works.
backups.verify: Press Scan now again, and write down the date of your last successful test restore.

steps: Put guest phones, smart TVs and cameras on a separate guest Wi-Fi (most routers have a 'Guest network' setting).
Keep office computers, servers and payment machines on the main network only.
Change the router's admin password from the default and update its firmware.
segmentation.verify: Press Scan now again from an office computer.

steps: Turn off old unencrypted services such as Telnet and FTP, and use SSH/SFTP instead.
For websites, turn on HTTPS (many hosts offer a free certificate with one click).
Turn on disk encryption: BitLocker / Device encryption on Windows, FileVault on macOS. Save the recovery key somewhere safe first.
Update the app, plugin or library named in the problem to its latest version.
Remove plugins and apps nobody uses.
Only install software from the official store or vendor website.
Plan to upgrade this system to a supported version, or replace the device. Many upgrades are free.
Until then, keep it off the internet, limit who can use it, and make sure it has a recent backup.
This is usually a job for your IT person or a professional, especially for servers.
unsupporteddev.verify: Press Scan now again after the upgrade.
